crockMaterials.name: Modern Certified Ceramic Crock (Post-1990s FDA Compliant)
crockMaterials.description: Manufactured under modern FDA CPG Sec 545.450 / California Prop 65 regulatory oversight using lead-free silicate glazes fired in high-temperature computer-controlled kilns.

crockMaterials.name: Modern Ceramic Crock with Glaze Crazing / Micro-Cracks
crockMaterials.description: Repetitive thermal shock cycles have caused fine microscopic hairline fractures (crazing) across the glaze. Hot acidic cooking broths penetrate beneath the vitreous glaze into the porous earthenware clay substrate.

crockMaterials.name: Vintage / Antique Slow Cooker Crock (Pre-1980s Manufacture)
crockMaterials.description: Produced prior to strict 1980s/1990s FDA pottery glaze enforcement. Vintage slow cookers frequently utilized low-fire flux glazes enriched with lead oxide (PbO) for gloss and yellow/red cadmium pigments.

crockMaterials.name: Traditional Artisanal / Uncertified Imported Earthenware (Barro)
crockMaterials.description: Handcrafted or unregulated imported pottery (such as traditional Mexican barro vidriado) fired at low temperatures with raw lead oxide (greta/litargirio) glazes. Highly reactive with food acids.

crockMaterials.name: Food-Grade 304/316 Stainless Steel Insert
crockMaterials.description: Non-ceramic metallic alloy vessel. Zero lead or cadmium glaze leaching. Chemically inert to organic acids up to 212°F (100°C), with negligible trace nickel/chromium release.

recipeAcidityProfiles.name: High-Acid Tomato Braise (pH 3.8 - 4.2: Marinara, Beef Chili)
recipeAcidityProfiles.description: Concentrated tomato sauces contain abundant citric and malic acids that actively chelate heavy metal cations from ceramic glazes under continuous heat.

recipeAcidityProfiles.name: Ultra-Acidic Vinegar / Wine Reduction (pH 3.0 - 3.5: Pulled Pork, Coq au Vin)
recipeAcidityProfiles.description: Aggressive low-pH organic acid environment. Acetic acid accelerates silicate dissolution and rapidly extracts unbound lead and cadmium into the braising liquid.

recipeAcidityProfiles.name: Moderate-Acid Stew (pH 5.0 - 5.5: Beef & Root Vegetable Stew)
recipeAcidityProfiles.description: Standard savory meat stew with root vegetables. Mildly acidic buffer with moderate heavy metal extraction potential.

recipeAcidityProfiles.name: Low-Acid Neutral Soup / Broth (pH 6.2 - 6.8: Bone Broth, Chicken Noodle)
recipeAcidityProfiles.description: Near-neutral aqueous environment. Heavy metal cation extraction is minimal, but prolonged danger-zone dwell times present significant microbial spore incubation risk.

recipeAcidityProfiles.name: Raw Red Kidney Bean Chili (Raw Soaked Phaseolus vulgaris) ⚠️
recipeAcidityProfiles.description: Contains toxic phytohaemagglutinin (PHA) lectin. If cooked at sub-boiling slow cooker temperatures (< 212°F / 100°C), PHA toxicity multiplies up to 500% compared to raw beans!

applianceSettings.name: LOW Setting (170°F - 195°F / 77°C - 90°C)
applianceSettings.description: Slow, gradual heating curve. Takes 3 to 4 hours to surpass the 140°F (60°C) microbial danger zone threshold. Never reaches 212°F (100°C) boiling.

applianceSettings.name: HIGH Setting (200°F - 212°F / 93°C - 100°C)
applianceSettings.description: Accelerated thermal ramp. Passes through the 40°F–140°F danger zone in under 2 hours, reaching a gentle simmer (205°F–210°F).

applianceSettings.name: KEEP WARM (Factory Calibrated: 150°F - 165°F / 65°C - 74°C)
applianceSettings.description: Safe post-cook holding temperature engineered above the USDA 140°F safety line to inhibit bacterial spore germination and vegetative proliferation.

applianceSettings.name: FAULTY / UNCALIBRATED WARM (< 130°F / 54°C) ⚠️
applianceSettings.description: Defective heating coil or overloaded cold contents holding food directly inside the optimal incubation zone (109°F–125°F) for Clostridium perfringens spore outgrowth.

startingTemperatures.name: Fully Thawed / Refrigerated (40°F / 4.4°C)
startingTemperatures.description: Ingredients thawed completely in the refrigerator as mandated by USDA-FSIS slow cooker safety guidelines.

startingTemperatures.name: Direct From Freezer Solid Block (0°F / -18°C) ⚠️
startingTemperatures.description: Direct insertion of large frozen meats or dense ice-crystallized blocks. Extends the core dwell time inside the 40°F–140°F danger zone by 2.5 to 4 extra hours.

toxicByproducts.name: Lead (Pb) Glaze Leaching
toxicByproducts.targetOrgans: Central nervous system, developing brain, hematologic (anemia), nephrotoxicity
toxicByproducts.vulnerableGroup: Pregnant women, fetuses, and children under 6 years (irreversible neurocognitive loss)
toxicByproducts.kinetics: Acidic hydrogen ions exchange with Pb cations in low-fired flux glaze, accelerated by continuous 180°F heat.

toxicByproducts.name: Cadmium (Cd) Pigment Leaching
toxicByproducts.targetOrgans: Renal proximal tubules (proteinuria), bone mineral density loss (Itai-itai disease)
toxicByproducts.vulnerableGroup: Chronic dietary consumers of acidic slow-cooked stews from glazed pottery
toxicByproducts.kinetics: Cadmium sulfide/selenide yellow/orange/red pigments leach under acidic hot liquid contact.

toxicByproducts.name: Phytohaemagglutinin (PHA Lectin)
toxicByproducts.standardLimit: < 400 HAU (Hemagglutinating Units in fully boiled beans)
toxicByproducts.targetOrgans: Small intestine brush border microvilli, mucosal cell death and hyper-secretion
toxicByproducts.vulnerableGroup: Anyone consuming unboiled or slow-cooked raw red kidney beans
toxicByproducts.kinetics: Raw beans contain 20,000–70,000 HAU. Cooking at 176°F (80°C) sub-boiling multiplies toxicity up to 500%.

toxicByproducts.name: Clostridium perfringens Spore Outgrowth
toxicByproducts.standardLimit: < 100 CFU/g (Infectious dose > 10⁶ CFU/g producing CPE enterotoxin)
toxicByproducts.targetOrgans: Lower gastrointestinal tract (severe watery diarrhea, intense cramping)
toxicByproducts.vulnerableGroup: Consumers of large meat roasts cooked slowly with long danger zone dwell times
toxicByproducts.kinetics: Heat-activated endospores germinate between 109°F–125°F with doubling times as short as 10 minutes.

toxicByproducts.name: Bacillus cereus Emetic Toxin (Cereulide)
toxicByproducts.standardLimit: Zero detectable cereulide toxin in ready-to-eat stews
toxicByproducts.targetOrgans: Stomach and upper GI tract (acute projectile vomiting within 1–5 hours)
toxicByproducts.vulnerableGroup: Consumers of starchy soups, rice, or potato stews left in warm/low temperature holding
toxicByproducts.kinetics: Spore germinates at 86°F–104°F and pre-forms cereulide, which survives 250°F (121°C) autoclaving for 90 minutes.

mitigationRules.title: Mandatory 10-Minute Rolling Boil for Red Kidney Beans
mitigationRules.summary: Never add raw or dried red kidney beans directly to a slow cooker. Soak dried beans in water for at least 5 hours, dump the soak water, and boil vigorously in fresh water at 212°F (100°C) for at least 10–30 minutes before adding to the cooker. Canned kidney beans are already commercially retort-cooked and 100% safe to add directly.

mitigationRules.title: Never Cook Large Frozen Roasts Directly in a Slow Cooker
mitigationRules.summary: Always thaw meat, poultry, and roasts completely in the refrigerator before placing them into the slow cooker. A solid frozen roast will take 4 to 6 hours for its core to reach 140°F (60°C), allowing heat-resistant Clostridium perfringens and Bacillus cereus spores to multiply unchecked and produce heat-stable toxins.

mitigationRules.title: Retire Crazed, Chipped, or Pre-1980s Vintage Cookware
mitigationRules.summary: Vintage crockpots (made before 1980) and uncertified artisanal pottery (e.g. traditional Mexican clay 'barro') frequently leach lead and cadmium at levels 10x to 100x above FDA limits when exposed to acidic tomatoes, wine, or vinegar. If a modern ceramic liner develops visible hairline spider-web cracking (crazing), replace the liner immediately.

mitigationRules.title: Verify 'Keep Warm' Temperature Stays Above 140°F (60°C)
mitigationRules.summary: Use a calibrated digital food thermometer to verify that your slow cooker holds broth at a minimum of 145°F–165°F (63°C–74°C) on the 'Keep Warm' setting. If temperature drops below 140°F, refrigerate leftovers immediately in shallow containers rather than leaving them in the pot for extended buffet holding.

mitigationRules.title: Use Rapid 'High' for the First Hour of Dense Stews
mitigationRules.summary: To shorten the time food spends in the 40°F–140°F (4°C–60°C) danger zone, start cooking dense stews and roasts on the 'High' setting for the first 60 minutes before switching to 'Low'. This drives core temperatures through the critical spore-incubation window more than twice as fast.
